column2: A map is **valid** when it is a locally finite map of the plane bounded by segments and circular arcs, **arcs of radius 1 allowed** (Condition 5 dropped), carrying a six-colouring in which no two interior points of one colour are at distance exactly 1. A **unit arc** is a boundary arc of radius 1; **(Q)** an arc whose centre carries both side colours and at least four colours; **(R2)** an arc whose centre carries the outer side colour and not the inner, with an inner-colour tile along the radius-2 circle over the whole arc. `M*` is a terminal valid modification (N2-TERM). `F(M)`: the vertices of at least four colours; `R(M)`: the vertices carrying a repeated colour.

Call a coloring scalable, if there is some small positive number eps such that the coloring remains unit-distance-free after you enlarge/shrink some of the tiles by at most eps. This is equivalent to the fact that the coloring avoids all distances in [1-eps,1+eps].

we assume that each face (i.e., arcwise connected component of S\G) has diameter less than 1, is homeomorphic to a disc, and is bounded by a cycle in G. Now a nice coloring of S obtained from G is a coloring such that each color class is the union of faces (and part of their boundaries) such that the distance between any two of these faces is greater than 1.
We define the map graph M = M(G, S) as the graph whose vertices are the faces of G such that two vertices in M are neighbors if and only if the corresponding facial cycles in G intersect.

Is there a valid six-map with unit arcs — equivalently, since every valid map has the property, one in which a vertex of at least four colours or a repeated colour lies within 3 of every point? **Exclude it** (the NO), or **build one** (the YES).
Every closed disc of radius 3 of every valid map holds a vertex of at least four colours or a vertex with a repeated colour.

In a valid map, if the closed disc of radius 2 about a cubic trichromatic vertex `u` holds no vertex of at least four colours and none with a repeated colour, row 134's base refutes the map near `u` (inert unit arcs centred within 1 of `u` first bent toward their centres).

In a valid map, a close complementary pair of cubic trichromatic vertices `u, u′` (disjoint multicolours, `d < 2`) sits on a unit rhombus `u, q₊, u′, q₋` whose other corners are vertices of at least four colours, each a leaving centre of both `u` and `u′`, a unit arc of each leaving centre's circle being both-kind there: T2 is forced at both common unit points.

In a valid map, every close complementary cubic trichromatic partner of a cubic trichromatic vertex `u` is the fourth corner `w_i + w_j − u` of a unit rhombus on two of `u`'s leaving centres, so `u` has at most three such partners.
The centre of a both-kind unit arc is a vertex with at least four colours or a repeated colour.
Every valid map has a valid modification by W-MERGE and whole-arc bends, creating no unit arc, in which every unit arc is (Q) or (R2); the procedure terminates with no stubs.

NB-4 corrected: at a vertex of exactly four colours, let `(v, y₀)` be a covering pair at a change point of its ring; if no point of `y₀`'s `σ_v`-orbit lies in the closure of an arc of `Γ` on `ω(v)`, and no arc of `Γ` on `ω(y_{k±1})` has `y_k` in its closure, contradiction; the bound on the colours at `y_k` is not needed.

A four-colour vertex with no covering pair on its unit circle has on that circle arcs of `Γ` centred at it of total length at least 60°, or at least six, one in each of six consecutive 60° windows (C-UA-BUDGET, branch 1).
A vertex with five colours has unit arcs centred at it of total length at least 180°; with six, its whole unit circle lies in `Γ`, every arc of kind both.

Every valid map has a valid modification `M*`, creating no unit arc, in which every unit arc is (Q) or (R2); every vertex is cubic, an NB4P exception with at least four colours, or stuck; every stuck vertex lies on a stuck chain along its normal line that is not bi-infinite, each finite end within distance 1 of a (Q) or (R2) arc or an NB4P exception, every horn bound `±1` on it a (Q) or (R2) arc; one-sided infinite chains are a GAP.

In a terminal valid map, the point of the normal line one step beyond each finite end of a stuck chain has at least four colours, except possibly beside a one-vertex chain bounded by unit arcs on both sides but not on all four horn arcs, at a bound on an (R2) arc — a residue not walked.

The two gaps compose as follows: (1) since every valid map has `F ∪ R` within 3 of every point, excluding such maps is the NO for every valid map, periodic or not, with no ray step; (2) for a doubly periodic map, the terminal modification's four-colour vertices meet every closed disc of radius `|K| + 2`, `K` its finite curvature set, so the NO reduces to the four-colour form with no ray step and no third step; (3) for aperiodic maps the four-colour form needs both the stuck ray excluded (b′) and a uniform bound on the length of finite stuck chains, a third GAP, (b″).

A doubly periodic valid map has a periodic terminal modification, so finitely many arc classes: it has no stuck ray and its chains are bounded; for a non-periodic map with finitely many arc classes whether its terminal modification keeps finitely many is a GAP, N3-ALPH.
